tagline: South along the old canal, from Delphos to the Loramie Summit.
intro: From Delphos the byway follows the line of the Miami and Erie Canal south through Spencerville, St. Marys, New Bremen and Minster toward Piqua, through farm country settled by Germans. The canal ran 274 miles from Cincinnati to Toledo and was finished in 1845, and the first settlers at Delphos were mostly men drawn there to build it.
Hands were scarce. Around New Bremen the subcontractors had to offer jiggers, two-ounce bottles of whiskey, to bring workers to the job.

moments.title: Grand Lake St. Marys
moments.text: Built as a feeder reservoir for the canal and once the largest man-made lake in the world, it had oil derricks standing out in the water by about 1891.

moments.title: New Bremen
moments.text: Restored canal locks and a lockkeeper's house stand downtown, at the north end of the Loramie Summit, the stretch that carried the canal to its highest ground.

moments.title: Lockington Locks
moments.text: Northbound boats were lifted 67 feet through these limestone locks, a passage of several hours, and the village of Lockington grew up to serve the idle boatmen.
